text: Chapter 2's finale — cleaning up what's been piling up all along. Vacuum.

Every update, delete, merge, and optimize leaves old files behind on disk — Lesson 17's point that a remove action doesn't delete a file right away. Those files aren't part of the current version, but they're not gone either — exactly what makes time travel possible.

Vacuum actually deletes them for good — but only files older than the retention window, seven days by default. Anything younger is left alone, specifically to protect time travel and any long-running query still reading an older version.

You can shorten that window, but it's genuinely risky — a long-running query mid-read on an older version can have its files deleted out from under it. This is exactly why time travel was never meant to be a permanent backup.

A transaction log, real ACID guarantees, schema enforcement, time travel, safe merges, and the maintenance to keep it all bounded — that's the whole chapter. Next: medallion architecture, putting every one of these tools to work.
